description: Minerva refined legacy attack pack — 28 focused techniques. Each script targets ONE specific flavour of its attack class; complements the Pro attacks. Every entry exposes configurable parameters for dynamic tuning.

attacks.name: Direct Prompt Injection
attacks.description: Role-hijack focused prompt injection (DAN / grandma / delimiter / override). Narrower than the Pro variant — four high-signal payloads with marker-co-occurrence confirmation. Use 'only_tool_names' to target specific tools.

attacks.name: Indirect Prompt Injection
attacks.description: Resource-focused audit — fetches every MCP resource and classifies hidden directives by technique (HTML comment, markdown title attribute, code-block delimiter escape, forced tool invocation).

attacks.name: Tool Poisoning
attacks.description: Laser-focused on invisible Unicode injection (zero-width, RTL override, directional formatting) in every metadata field — tool name, description, parameter docs, prompt args, resource descriptions.

attacks.name: Tool Shadowing
attacks.description: Description-collision detection via text similarity (difflib ratio). Flags tool pairs whose descriptions are near-duplicates and could confuse LLM routing.

attacks.name: Tool Name Conflict
attacks.description: Exact duplicate + case/punct-variant name collisions (read-file vs Read_File). Pure static analysis — no network calls beyond the tools/list discovery.

check_case_variants.description: Flag case/punct variants of the same name

attacks.name: Tool Misuse via Malicious Metadata
attacks.description: Detects 'use instead: X', fake deprecation banners, and forced prerequisite/follow-up calls in tool descriptions — metadata-level trust exploits.

attacks.name: Tool Preference Manipulation
attacks.description: Flags persuasive language in tool descriptions ('preferred', 'recommended', 'always use', 'never use X') that biases LLM tool-selection.

attacks.name: Tool Coverage Hijacking
attacks.description: Flags tools with vague / broad descriptions that could intercept LLM routing from more specific siblings.

min_description_words.description: Shorter descriptions are flagged as vague

attacks.name: Schema Inconsistencies
attacks.description: Sends intentionally wrong-typed values (int where string declared, etc.) and flags tools that accept them — schema validation missing.

attacks.name: Slash Command Overlap
attacks.description: Flags tool names that normalise to common client slash-commands (/help, /reset, /clear, /compact, /auth, etc.) — command hijacking vector.

extra_reserved_names.description: Additional names to treat as reserved

attacks.name: ConfusedAI Tool Misuse
attacks.description: Detects tools whose name suggests one verb class (read, list, get, view, check) but whose description mentions the opposite class (write, delete, modify) — semantic mismatch misroutes dangerous calls.

attacks.name: Multi-Tool Cooperation
attacks.description: Cross-tool exploit chain: writes a canary via a write-tool, reads via a read-tool. If the canary surfaces unsanitised, attacker-controlled data crosses trust boundaries.

attacks.name: Infectious Attack
attacks.description: Tests multi-hop state propagation: plant a canary via tool A, retrieve via tool B. Proves attacker-controlled state crosses tool boundaries within the LLM context.

attacks.name: MCP Credential Theft
attacks.description: Scans every resource and tool-default response for credential patterns: API keys (OpenAI, Anthropic, Slack, GitHub, AWS, GCP), JWTs, private keys, DB URLs with embedded passwords.

attacks.name: Vulnerable Client
attacks.description: Probes MCP server version-handling: accepts obsolete protocolVersion? leaks client-upgrade warnings?

attacks.name: Configuration Drift
attacks.description: Samples server capabilities / tool list / resource list N times and flags drift between snapshots — inconsistent backend replicas or active tampering.

attacks.name: File-Based Injection (Addition)
attacks.description: Detects arbitrary file-write tools. Writes a canary file at a configurable path, reads it back, confirms round-trip.

sandbox_path.description: Directory to write canary files (use forward-slash; /tmp works on Linux/Mac; set to 'C:/Windows/Temp' for Windows MCPs)

attacks.name: File-Based Injection (Deletion)
attacks.description: Tests for file-delete primitive by attempting to delete a non-existent file and checking whether the server distinguishes 'not found' (bad) from 'forbidden' (good).

attacks.name: File-Based Injection (Modification)
attacks.description: Confirms file-overwrite semantics: writes v1, writes v2, reads back and checks the newer version won.

attacks.name: File-Based Injection (Retrieval)
attacks.description: Probes directory-listing tools with common Linux/Windows paths + wildcards. Flags tools that enumerate the real filesystem.

attacks.name: MCP Server Backdoor Discovery
attacks.description: Enumerates tools for backdoor-like names/descriptions (admin, debug, wipe, raw-exec, bypass, impersonate) — exposed operator-grade capabilities. Supports org-specific custom patterns.

attacks.name: Package Name Squatting
attacks.description: Checks server-reported serverInfo.name against a known-good list using string similarity — flags near-match typosquatting.

min_similarity.description: Ratio above which names are considered suspicious

extra_known_packages.description: Additional legitimate packages to include in the corpus

attacks.name: Remote Code Execution (eval fuzz)
attacks.description: Non-OOB variant: sends arithmetic expressions in Python/Node/Ruby/PHP and scans response for known output markers. Faster than the Pro RCE but lower confidence.

attacks.name: SQL Injection (error-based)
attacks.description: Pure error-based SQLi fuzz with 11 error-triggering payloads and 30+ DB error markers (sqlite, mysql, postgres, mssql, oracle, odbc). Faster than the layered Pro variant.

attacks.name: Server Code Leakage
attacks.description: Triggers a malformed JSON-RPC call and scans error responses + tool responses for source-code fragments (Python def, JS function, PHP tags, stack-frame paths).

attacks.name: MCP Man In The Middle
attacks.description: ACTIVE variant: spawns Minerva's mitm_proxy in front of the target, captures MCP flows, audits them for auth leakage + credential bodies.

capture_seconds.description: How long to leave the proxy running

attacks.name: MCP Tool Rebinding (race)
attacks.description: Functional TOCTOU race: hammers tools/list in a background thread while exercising tools. Fingerprint-over-time uniqueness proves runtime-vs-audit divergence.

attacks.name: Command Injection (metacharacter fuzz)
attacks.description: Response-echo variant: sends classic metacharacter payloads and scans for shell-output markers (uid=, root:, Windows markers). No OOB/timing — fast and loud.
